title: Artificial intelligence in physical therapy
summary:
Artificial intelligence in physical therapy refers to the integration of AI technologies into physical and mental rehabilitation, with the potential to significantly transform these fields. AI applications such as natural language processing, computer vision, virtual reality, machine learning, and robotics are shaping the future of physical and mental recovery.

AI technology can be utilized in the diagnosis and assessment process by assisting physical therapists to make the process easier and more efficient. It is also improving physical therapy operations behind the scenes by helping with tasks like scheduling, documentation, billing and coding, and compliance. AI plays an increasingly greater role in evaluations, treatment planning, goal setting, and tracking patient progress.

Through the use of wearable devices and motion analysis, AI allows physical therapists to remotely monitor patients, enabling adjustments to care plans without the need for in-person visits. This is particularly beneficial for healthcare delivery in remote or underserved areas. Wearable devices equipped with AI offer further insights into patient activity levels, continuously monitoring physical activity and providing therapists with up-to-the-minute data on patient progress.

AI also has potential in neurologic physiotherapy. Computer-aided diagnosis systems using AI and modern signal processing methods have the ability to help clinicians in analyzing and interpreting physiological signals and images more effectively in neurological disorders such as epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and ischemic brain stroke.

Rather than replacing physical therapists, AI can assist by easing their workload and enabling greater focus on patients, leading to more personalized and effective care. Several concerns have been raised about the adoption of AI in rehabilitation, including patient privacy and ethical considerations. Researchers emphasize the importance of establishing guidelines when incorporating AI in rehabilitation.
